title: An optimal ALMA image of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field in the era of JWST: obscured star formation and the cosmic far-infrared background
question: Combine all archival ALMA Band 6 data on the HUDF into the deepest 1.23 mm map, catalogue the dusty star-forming galaxies and their JWST/HST counterparts, and measure how much of the cosmic infrared background at 1.23 mm is resolved by detections plus stacking

data.angular_resolution: Deep map: 1.49 x 1.07 arcsec (250 klambda taper); 1.32 x 0.92 arcsec (no taper). Wide map: 0.87 x 0.64 arcsec (tapered); 0.36 x 0.27 arcsec (no taper)
data.sensitivity: Deep map minimum rms 4.6 uJy/beam, rms < 9.0 uJy/beam over 1.5 arcmin^2, < 35 uJy/beam over all 4.2 arcmin^2; wide map typical rms 60 uJy/beam outside and 20 uJy/beam within individual pointings

recipe.goal: retrieve and calibrate archival uv data
recipe.method: Query the ALMA archive for Band 6 data within 1.5 arcmin of the HUDF centre, download raw data, calibrate with the provided scriptForPI, split science targets, time-average and channel-average
key_parameters: time averaging 30 s; frequency channel averaging factor 4

recipe.method: Image all averaged uv data jointly with tclean in MFS mode with natural weighting and a 250 klambda taper (also untapered and uniform-noise variants), for a deep central map and a wider shallower map
key_parameters: pixel 0.2 arcsec (deep tapered), primary beam cutoff 0.2; wide map pixel 0.12 arcsec, cutoff 0.4
assumptions: No correction for spectral variation across about 30 per cent bandwidth

recipe.method: Mask known galaxies from published catalogues, compute rms in cutouts around each pixel of the masked map, smooth the result
key_parameters: mask 3 x beamsize; rms cutout 5 x beamsize; Gaussian smoothing with kernel equal to cutout size

recipe.goal: detect sources and set the threshold
recipe.method: Run peak finding on the S/N map and its negative; choose the threshold by purity = 1 - N_neg/N_pos
key_parameters: purity 0.7 corresponds to peak S/N = 3.6; 45 sources above threshold
assumptions: Source extraction relies on Gaussian noise; negative peaks used as the false-positive proxy

recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian with position and amplitude fixed at the peak pixel, derive number of beams, integrated flux S1230 = S_peak x N_b if N_b > 1 else peak pixel
key_parameters: wide map: peak pixel used above 1000 uJy and a 2 arcsec aperture for ALMA-HUDF-69

recipe.method: Match published sources within 1 arcsec; scale Dunlop et al. and GOODS-ALMA flux densities to 243 GHz with a modified blackbody
key_parameters: beta = 1.8, Td = 25 K, galaxy redshift or z = 1.5 if unknown; GOODS-ALMA correction factor 0.8
assumptions: modified blackbody SED beta = 1.8, Td = 25 K

recipe.goal: match ALMA sources to JADES and CANDELS counterparts
recipe.method: Search JADES within 1.9 arcsec/(S/N) (minimum 0.3 arcsec); CANDELS within a uniform 0.6 arcsec after applying a 0.25 arcsec southward offset; checked by eye
assumptions: 2.5 x radial positional uncertainty gives 95 per cent correct matches

recipe.goal: derive photometric redshifts and stellar masses (JADES)
recipe.method: Dual-image SExtractor photometry with TPHOT for lower-resolution bands, then LePhare SED fitting; spectroscopic redshifts fixed where known
key_parameters: two metallicities (0.2 Zsun, Zsun); exponentially declining star-formation histories with tau 0.1 to 15 Gyr
assumptions: Bruzual-Charlot templates, Chabrier IMF, Calzetti attenuation law

recipe.goal: stack JADES galaxies in the ALMA map
recipe.method: Mask ALMA-detected sources, subtract the weighted mean, convolve hits maps of each stellar-mass and redshift bin with the ALMA beam, and solve a weighted linear regression for each bin amplitude
key_parameters: four stellar mass bins, 7.4 to 11.4 in log10(M*/Msun), width 1 dex
four redshift bins between 0 and 8, width 2
source mask of 3 x FWHM diameter
assumptions: Redshift bins are wide enough that clustering correlations between bins are negligible, so bins are fit independently

recipe.method: Add detected-source flux (above 3.6 sigma), the stacked flux (S_hat x N_eff summed over bins), and a bright-source term from GOODS-ALMA for S1230 > 0.85 mJy
key_parameters: detected area 1.15e-3 deg^2; stack area 1.11e-3 deg^2
assumptions: No additional bright (above 0.85 mJy) sources in the map, so the GOODS-ALMA count is added as a constant

recipe.goal: estimate the absolute CIB at the effective map frequency
recipe.method: Compute the map transmission function from inverse-variance weights of uniform-coverage programmes, derive nu_eff with the FIRAS modified blackbody, then derive the CIB amplitude from the FIRAS fit or a power-law interpolation of Planck CIB at 217 and 353 GHz
key_parameters: beta = 0.65, Td = 18.5 K fixed; nu_eff = 241.4 GHz; 10,000 Gaussian draws
assumptions: Each observation's transmission is flat across its two sidebands; CIB spectral shape fixed

recipe.goal: test consistency of the measured CIB with the absolute CIB using SIDES fluctuations
recipe.method: Take random HUDF-sized patches from a SIDES 1 deg^2 tile to get fractional fluctuations, then compare the measured CIB with Monte Carlo draws of the absolute CIB and fluctuation amplitude
key_parameters: patches of 4.2 arcmin^2; fluctuation delta I / I = 17 per cent; 10,000 Gaussian draws
assumptions: No fluctuations from the S1230 > 0.85 mJy population (treated as a constant) and no contribution from galaxies below the stacking mass limit

recipe.method: Convolve the archive MFS images to a common beam, reproject to a common grid, build noise maps, and combine with inverse-variance weights and edge apodization; compare detections with the uv-combined map
key_parameters: common beam from the largest beam; 0.2 arcsec grid spanning 5 arcmin; Gaussian apodization with sigma equal to beamsize out to 3 x beamsize
